items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: I've known him ever since, but I don't know [how he came up].

ctx.x: Sullivan doesn't show that immediate influence. Sullivan shows the vitality without the figuration being so nearly identical. And then of course there have been the Stacey disciples after that moment.
When I again talk about Chicago pianos, I drop out Joe, only because I really don't associate him with Chicago. That record in 26 was the first really driving piano that ever came out of Chicago.

Well then he joined these Chicago fellows with Red Nickels and then he gradually becomes a Chicago. Yeah. By, but he does come out of the clear, the clear blue. You don't know quite how he happened to get into, amongst the Chicago fellows. I hope I get a talk with him and discover his first contact with Chicago.
